cards.proposedFrench: le cours / la salle de classe
cards.proposalNote: Session: le cours, as in Reader line 1. Room: la salle de classe, as in Reader line 7. The two senses are not interchangeable.
French est covers identity, condition and location. This Reader has no identity example. Keep this source English card separate under its stable number; no scoring policy is enabled.
French est covers condition and location. Reader lines 2 and 3 attest location; no condition example is present. Do not treat se trouve as a condition form.
Il y a works for singular and plural.
Mainly the feminine article here; it can also be an object pronoun.
Un is masculine; une is feminine.

candidateGrammar.explanation: French nouns have grammatical gender. Learn the article with the noun: le cahier, un livre (masculine); la table, la chaise, une table (feminine). French est can describe identity, condition or location. Use il y a for there is or there are, sur for on a surface, dans for inside, and près de for near. In the source sentences, bleu follows masculine nouns: un livre bleu, le sac à dos est bleu. De and je shorten before a vowel: d’un, j’ai. Here la is mainly the feminine article.
